newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse index edges up to new high.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse index edges up to new high.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index edged up into new record territory on Tuesday but a calmer note on foreign markets has left its impact on the Hungarian market too, traders said.
"I expect the pace of the recent rise to slow down," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities. "The rally, we saw earlier this year, cannot be maintained."
The BUX index finished in the second new record high in a row, at 4,749.26 points, but up only 6.56 points as early losses chopped later gains.

"Before the launch of trading on the Budapest bourse, prices of Hungarian stocks were not very encouraging on the SEAQ...and the Hungarian bourse opened with price falls dominating the market," Lencs said.
However, most early losses shifted to gains later and these rises pushed up a few stocks, including tile manufacturer Zalakeramia and chemicals maker Borsodchem to record grounds.
Zalakeramia rallied to a new record level of 8,500 forints rapidly as the market reacted positively on its most recent news of acquisition plans.

"The announcement of the acquisition plans definitely explain the current price increase," a trader said earlier today. "Should further information be released on the deals Zalakeramia share price may rise further."
Later its price softened but by the close it had rebounded to finish at 8,500, up 350.
Zalakeramia will hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting on February 12 to discuss issues related to its planned new acquisitions. It said three companies were of serious interest.
Chemicals maker Borsodchem was the day's other strong gainer. In active trade it rose to a new record high of 4,800 forints but later it eased to finish at 4,715, up 220.
Elsewhere on the market the pharmaceuticals stocks closed mixed, with Richter dipping 140 forints to 10,450, Egis rising 250 forints to 10,150 and Human firming 50 forints to 3,050.
Hotel stocks ended mixed with Danubius losing 3.3 percent or 145 fofints to end at 4,245 forints, while Eravis remained steady in one single deal.
Beverages companies closed higher with the exception of brewery Martfu which dipped 20 forints to 2,330.
